title: Models ship meshopt-packed and the big landmarks swap between a derived far tier and their near tier by camera distance
context: Owner: swap game-ready and extreme-low tiers by distance; build the swap with the upstream d3 tiers as stand-ins; try meshopt compression; is a game-ready solar still needed? Found: the upstream d1-d3 files are damage states with the same triangle counts (Terraformer d3 39.6k vs 40.5k), useless as far tiers; gltfpack's simplifier at -si 0.1 -sa gives real far tiers (solar 131k -> 7.1k triangles); plain -si without -sa barely reduces (borders locked).
outcome: scripts/build.mjs packs every assets/models/*.glb into dist with gltfpack (-cc -kn -km -ke); sources and their upstream locks untouched; gltfpack is a dev dependency and both workflows run npm ci. All nine GLTFLoader sites set the vendored meshopt decoder. dist models 89 MB -> 14.9 MB, release 29 MB. scripts/far-tiers.mjs (npm run tiers) derives far tiers for structures with a `far` field (solar, hugin, stalheart, assembly) and pins source and derived hashes in docs/far-tier-assets.lock.json, verified by the asset check. story-base loads the far tier first, fetches the near tier only within KIT.lod.metres (150 m) and swaps by camera distance with 1.3x hysteresis; the game and the lab pass the camera. Lab acceptance checks all far from the overview and the solar near tier loading up close. The release acceptance allows the packed MÖRK's triangle count within 1 % (degenerate triangles dropped). The owner then exported the solar complex as LOD1 (3,856 triangles, 7 draws, 340 KB) and LOD2 (2,752, 1 draw, 237 KB): pinned in docs/solar-lod-assets.lock.json as the solar near and far tiers; the derived far tier is kept only for hugin, stalheart and assembly. A dist run exposed that a tank model landing mid roll-out rebuilt the actors and emptied the life containers: in the story they now outlive an actor rebuild and the clip deploy holds its own bay handle. docs/ASSET-COLLABORATION.md is the export contract and budget sheet for the assets manager.
alternatives: Upstream d3 files as far tiers: rejected, they are damage states of the same detail.
Committing packed copies next to the sources: rejected, path churn and duplicate bytes; packing the release copy keeps the pinned provenance intact.
A game-ready solar export: no longer needed for bytes (333 KB packed); still worth asking for if phones stutter near the solar island (131k triangles at the near tier).
evidence: npm run tiers: solar 9.20 MB/131236 tris -> 286 KB/7136; hugin -> 142 KB/4492; stalheart -> 790 KB/4998; assembly -> 1213 KB/6708
npm test 92, npm run check (far tiers verified), npm run build 29.3 MB
browser: --story PASS with the LOD checks; --dist, --dist --story, --dist --story-world run before commit
